messages:
Eli (customer): Hey team — we started hitting a bunch of 429s this morning during our nightly CI run. We're on the free tier and saw requests fail across multiple services. Anyone able to advise?
Maya (support): Sorry about that, Eli. Can you paste one failing request id or a curl example? Also does this happen only during the nightly job or during normal usage too?
Eli (customer): Only the nightly ingest. It's a bunch of parallel jobs spinning up and each job uses the same API key. Example error: "rate_limit_exceeded" and the response included Retry-After: 60.
Maya (support): Got it. Free plan has a short burst window and a concurrency ceiling per account. If many CI workers reuse the same key you'll exceed the concurrent in-flight request limit quickly. Can you confirm how many parallel workers you run?
Eli (customer): ~30 concurrent runners, each doing several small /v1/generate calls. We can change config but need a short-term fix while we rework CI.
Jess (sre): 30 concurrency on a single free key will hit the quota. Short-term options: 1) reduce parallelism, 2) add per-worker exponential backoff with jitter, 3) use multiple keys (separate service accounts) to spread concurrency. Also we can repro with a simple curl flood: 
```
for i in {1..40}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}' &
done
wait
```
You should see 429 responses and headers like `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` or `Retry-After`.
Maya (support): For an immediate customer-facing workaround we can issue a temporary demo uplift for 24 hours (sales needs to approve) so you don't have CI breakage while you implement backoffs. Samir, can you advise on a short-term quota bridge?
Samir (sales): Yep, I can approve a 48h temporary uplift to the paid trial bucket for this account if support confirms the customer and provides the account id. This is a one-time emergency uplift — we'll flag for conversion follow-up. Eli, can you DM me the account email?
Eli (customer): Sent the email via DM. Thanks. Also curious — any recommended target limits for parallel workers after we fix CI?
Jess (sre): Recommend aiming for no more than 8 concurrent in-flight requests per API key on shared tiers to avoid head-of-line limits. With batching or caching you can often cut token volumes too. For higher sustained throughput switch to Dedicated or a paid plan that allows reserved concurrency and predictable SLAs.
Maya (support): Next steps: 1) We (support) will create the temporary uplift once Sales confirms (Samir approved 48h). 2) Eli to implement per-worker backoff and/or split keys. 3) Jess to add a short KB snippet on CI best practices for concurrent runs. I'll follow up with the uplift ticket id here. :thumbsup:
support-bot: UPLIFT-REQ-5602 created, assigned to Samir (sales).
Samir (sales): Uplift created and applied; Eli should have increased headroom now. Please monitor and confirm. I'll also loop a solutions engineer for an optional short workshop on rate design if they want to move to a dedicated tier.
Eli (customer): Confirmed — CI runs are succeeding now. We'll implement the backoff and split keys in the next sprint. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
note: single-thread Slack conversation; messages in chronological order
